source_refs.note: Exercise 3.3, Question 14: book p. 89-90, 24 questions (integration by parts); answer key p. 301 (printed under 'Exercise 3.5')

blocks.explanation:
Split into \(\int \frac{\cos x}{x}\,dx - \int \frac{\sin x}{x^2}\,dx\); neither can be done alone.
Plan: integrate the second by parts (\(\sin x\) first, \(x^{-2}\) second); the \(\int \frac{\cos x}{x}\,dx\) terms cancel.
steps:
Given: \(\int \frac{x\cos x - \sin x}{x^2}\,dx\), \(x \ne 0\).
To find: the indefinite integral.
Method: split; integrate \(\int \sin x\cdot x^{-2}\,dx\) by parts with \(\sin x\) first and \(x^{-2}\) second.

Split
\[= \int \dfrac{\cos x}{x}\,dx - \int \dfrac{\sin x}{x^2}\,dx\]
Why: divide each term of the numerator by \(x^2\).

Parts on the second integral
\[\int \sin x\cdot x^{-2}\,dx = \sin x\left(-\dfrac{1}{x}\right) - \int \left(-\dfrac{1}{x}\right)\cos x\,dx\]
\[= -\dfrac{\sin x}{x} + \int \dfrac{\cos x}{x}\,dx\]
Why: \(\int x^{-2}\,dx = -\frac{1}{x}\); \(\frac{d}{dx}\sin x = \cos x\).

Substitute back: cancellation
\[= \int \dfrac{\cos x}{x}\,dx + \dfrac{\sin x}{x} - \int \dfrac{\cos x}{x}\,dx\]
\[= \dfrac{\sin x}{x} + c\]
Why: the two integrals cancel.

Check
\[\dfrac{d}{dx}\left(\dfrac{\sin x}{x}\right) = \dfrac{x\cos x - \sin x\cdot 1}{x^2}\]
Why: quotient rule gives the integrand.
